subject: Agriculture
title: Biological Crop Protection
description: A micro-lesson that makes Biological Crop Protection usable.

hook.text: A fungus called Beauveria bassiana kills pest insects from the inside. It's nature's pesticide—no synthetic chemicals needed.

buildup.text: Biological pesticides—or biopesticides—use living organisms or natural compounds to control pests and diseases.

discovery.text: The biopesticide market grows 15% annually. By 2030, it could capture 25% of the crop protection market.

twist.text: Biopesticides break down quickly in the environment—fewer residues, but they also require more precise timing to work.

climax.text: RNA interference technology sprays RNA that silences specific pest genes—killing only the target insect.

punchline.text: Kill the pest, spare everything else. Biology targets better than chemistry.

quiz.question: How fast is the biopesticide market growing annually?
